title: 157. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Detecting Truncated Graph Axes
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify whether a graph uses a truncated vertical axis.
questions.question: A bar graph compares two values. The vertical axis starts at \(50\), and the bars reach \(60\) and \(70\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The graph is not truncated because both bars are drawn accurately.

options.label: B
options.text: The graph is truncated because the vertical axis does not start at zero.

questions.explanation: A truncated vertical axis occurs when the vertical axis does not begin at zero or omits part of the scale. Here the vertical axis starts at \(50\), so the graph is truncated. This can make the difference between \(60\) and \(70\) look larger than it really is. Therefore, the correct statement is B.
questions.hint: Check whether the vertical axis begins at zero or at another value.

questions.learningObjective: Identify visual features that indicate a truncated vertical axis.
questions.question: Which feature most directly indicates that a graph may have a truncated vertical axis?

options.label: A
options.text: The vertical axis starts at a non-zero value or contains a break.

options.label: B
options.text: The horizontal axis uses equal intervals.

questions.explanation: Truncation is a property of the vertical scale. A vertical axis that starts at a non-zero value or contains a break omits part of the scale, so it may be truncated. Equal intervals on the horizontal axis do not by themselves indicate a truncated vertical axis. Therefore, A is correct.
questions.hint: Think about what a truncated axis leaves out, and which visible feature of a graph would show that something has been left out.

questions.concept: Effect of a Truncated Axis on Visual Comparison
questions.learningObjective: Determine how a truncated axis affects the perceived difference between values.
questions.question: A graph's vertical axis runs from \(90\) to \(100\). Two bars have values \(94\) and \(98\). What is the main effect of this axis range?

options.label: A
options.text: It accurately shows that the difference is small.

options.label: B
options.text: It visually exaggerates the difference between the two values.

questions.explanation: The actual difference between \(94\) and \(98\) is \(4\) units. On a vertical axis from \(90\) to \(100\), the bar for \(94\) occupies a noticeable portion of the axis and the bar for \(98\) occupies a much larger portion. This makes the difference appear larger than it is. Therefore, the truncated axis exaggerates the visual difference, so B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the actual numerical difference with the fraction of the vertical axis each bar occupies.

questions.concept: Comparing Graphs with Different Axis Starts
questions.learningObjective: Select which graph is more likely to exaggerate small differences.
questions.question: Two bar graphs show the same data. One vertical axis starts at \(0\), and the other starts at \(80\). Which graph is more likely to exaggerate small differences between values near \(90\)?

options.label: A
options.text: The graph with the axis starting at \(0\).

options.label: B
options.text: The graph with the axis starting at \(80\).

questions.explanation: A vertical axis starting at \(80\) truncates the scale and compresses the visible range. Values near \(90\) then occupy a large portion of the axis, so small numerical differences appear visually large. A vertical axis starting at \(0\) shows the data on a full scale and does not exaggerate in this way. Therefore, B is correct.
questions.hint: Consider how much of the vertical axis is used to show the region containing the data.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the meaning of a break in a graph axis.
questions.question: A line graph has a break symbol on the vertical axis between \(0\) and \(100\), then continues from \(100\) to \(110\). What does this break most likely indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: Some data values are missing from the graph.

options.label: B
options.text: Part of the vertical scale has been omitted.

questions.explanation: A break symbol on an axis indicates that a section of the scale has been omitted so that the graph can show a narrower range. It does not mean that data values are missing. Since the vertical scale skips from \(0\) to \(100\), part of the vertical scale has been omitted. Therefore, B is correct.
questions.hint: Consider what an axis break changes: the plotted data values, or the range of values that the axis displays.

questions.concept: Calculating Actual Difference from a Truncated Graph
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the actual difference between two values shown on a truncated axis.
questions.question: A bar graph uses a vertical axis from \(100\) to \(120\). The two bars have values \(105\) and \(115\). What is the actual difference between the two values?
questions.explanation:
The actual difference between the two values is found from the data values, not from the axis range:
\[
115-105=10
\]
The vertical axis from \(100\) to \(120\) may affect how large the difference appears, but it does not change the actual difference. Therefore, the actual difference is \(10\) units, so A is correct.
questions.hint: Decide which numbers are the data values and which numbers only describe the scale of the axis.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how truncation changes the perceived size of an increase.
questions.question: A graph shows a value increasing from \(98\) to \(100\). The vertical axis starts at \(95\). How does this truncated axis affect perception?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes the increase appear much larger than it actually is.

options.label: B
options.text: It makes the increase appear smaller than it actually is.

questions.explanation: The actual increase is \(100-98=2\) units, which is only about \(2\%\) of \(98\). Measured from the axis start of \(95\), the plotted heights are \(98-95=3\) and \(100-95=5\), so the plotted height grows by about \(67\%\). This makes the increase appear much larger than it actually is. Therefore, A is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the numerical increase with the portion of the vertical axis used to display it.

questions.concept: Recovering an Actual Value from Bar Heights
questions.learningObjective: Determine an actual data value from bar heights drawn on a truncated vertical axis.
questions.question: A bar graph's vertical axis starts at \(40\). The shorter bar has the value \(46\), and the taller bar is drawn \(4\) times as tall as the shorter bar. What is the actual value of the taller bar?
questions.explanation: Bar heights on this graph are measured from the axis start of \(40\). The shorter bar is \(46-40=6\) units tall, so the taller bar is \(4\times 6=24\) units tall. Its actual value is \(40+24=64\). The value \(184\) comes from \(4\times 46\), which would be correct only if the axis started at zero. Therefore, A is correct.
questions.hint: First work out how tall the shorter bar is drawn on this graph, then use the factor \(4\).

questions.concept: Visual Ratio versus Actual Ratio under Truncation
questions.learningObjective: Compare visual ratio with actual ratio when the axis is truncated.
questions.question: A graph's vertical axis starts at \(200\). Two bars have values \(210\) and \(220\). On the graph, the \(220\) bar appears about twice as tall as the \(210\) bar. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The graph shows the true ratio of the two values.

options.label: B
options.text: The graph exaggerates the difference because the axis starts at \(200\).

questions.explanation:
The actual ratio of the values is:
\[
\frac{220}{210}\approx 1.05
\]
However, the graph measures bar heights from the axis start of \(200\). The heights above the axis are \(210-200=10\) and \(220-200=20\), so the visual ratio is \(20\div 10=2\). Thus the graph exaggerates the difference. Therefore, B is correct.
questions.hint: Find the ratio of the bar heights measured from the axis start, then compare it with the ratio of the actual values.

questions.concept: Definition of a Truncated Graph Axis
questions.learningObjective: Identify the best description of a truncated graph axis.
questions.question: Which statement best describes a truncated graph axis?

options.label: A
options.text: It does not start at zero or omits part of the scale, which can make differences appear larger.

options.label: B
options.text: It always starts at zero and therefore shows exact proportional differences.

questions.explanation: A truncated graph axis does not begin at zero or skips part of the scale. Because the visible range is reduced, differences between values can appear larger than they are. A non-truncated axis that starts at zero shows the full scale and does not create this particular distortion. Therefore, A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall what value a full, non-truncated vertical axis usually starts at.
